name: ABS reports 2004-05 onwards as FINANCIAL years (Jul-Jun). Convention used here: a financial year is mapped to its START calendar year, i.e. the year the reference period opens and the year containing the mid-point (~Dec/Jan).
internet1999: 1998-2003 columns are ABS's own calendar-year labels (single-enumeration surveys, not financial years) - carried through unchanged.

name: internet2009, internet2011, internet2013, internet2015 are EMPTY for every state: the HUIT survey went BIENNIAL from 2010-11, so there is no 2009-10, 2011-12, 2013-14 or 2015-16 collection.
internet1998: internet2003 is EMPTY for NT only (ABS did not publish that cell).
internet1999: NOTHING in this file is interpolated. Empty means no ABS estimate exists.

name: The 1998-2003 points come from DIFFERENT survey vehicles, per 8146.0 2008-09 Explanatory Notes para 6: Population Survey Monitor (1998, 1999, 2000); Survey of Education, Training and Information Technology (2001); General Social Survey (2002, face-to-face); Survey of Disability, Ageing and Carers (2003).
internet1998: MPHS (Multipurpose Household Survey, telephone, Jul-Jun accumulation) is the vehicle from 2004-05 onward.
internet1999: TREAT 1998-2003 vs 2004-onward as a SERIES BREAK; ABS states SDAC/MPHS are comparable at the HOUSEHOLD level (para 14) but the 2002 GSS face-to-face-to-telephone mode change 'cannot be ruled out' as affecting responses (para 15).

name: 8146.0 2008-09 Explanatory Notes para 13: from the 2005-06 MPHS onward the person scope is 15+; earlier collections were 18+. ABS says data before/after are 'not directly comparable'.
internet1998: This is a PERSON-level scope change; the household-level measure in this file is less affected but the 2004-05/2005-06 step should not be read as pure diffusion.

name: The measure itself is stable across the whole span: 'household has internet access at home', any connection type. It is NOT the broadband series (8146.0 publishes broadband separately; broadband would be a genuine definitional break and is deliberately excluded here).
internet1998: Denominator is total households in the state/territory in each cycle, as published by ABS.

name: 1998-2006 are published to the nearest whole per cent (rounding error up to +-0.5pp); 2007-2016 are published to one decimal. Mixed precision within a row is a source-precision artefact, not a data change.
internet1998: Relative standard errors are published in companion RSE cubes (81460DO002_* / Chapter-2-RSE cubes); typical RSE on the state internet-access proportion is 1-2% for NSW/VIC/QLD/WA/SA, 2-4% TAS, 2-3% ACT, 3-7% NT.

name: The 8146.0 series CEASED after 2016-17. For a 2015-2019 drift window only internet2014 (2014-15) and internet2016 (2016-17) exist; there is NO ABS household-internet state series for 2017, 2018 or 2019.
internet1998: For a 2006-2010 window: internet2006, internet2007, internet2008, internet2010 exist (2009 does not).
